title: Centralized Container Governance for Global Logistics
business: A global logistics firm managing distributed microservices across multiple regions needs a unified way to store and distribute container images.
problem: The firm faces fragmented image storage, inconsistent access controls, and security risks from using disparate, unmanaged registries that lack centralized audit trails.
solution: Artifact Registry provides a single, secure, and managed repository for container images and language packages, enabling granular IAM controls and native integration with Google Cloud security services.
steps: Create a standard Artifact Registry repository in a central project.
Configure IAM roles to grant developers read/write access based on the principle of least privilege.
Integrate the registry with CI/CD pipelines to automatically push validated images.
Enable vulnerability scanning to ensure only compliant images are deployed to production.
outcome: The organization achieves a unified, secure supply chain with consistent access policies and improved visibility into software components.
limitation: Artifact Registry storage costs scale with usage; users must monitor repository size and implement lifecycle policies to delete old or unused images to manage storage footprint.
